newsitem.title: USA: Private firm joins Phoenix Network in merge.
newsitem.headline: Private firm joins Phoenix Network in merge.

text.p: Resurgens Capital Group Inc is joining Phoenix Network Inc in its planned merger with US ONE Communications Corp to create a national switch-based long distance company and competitive local exchange carrier.

John Phillips, the former president and chief executive of Metromedia International Group Inc who controls Resurgens, will become chairman and chief executive of the new combined entity, the companies said.

Resurgens, a private company, was formed to pursue investment opportunities in the telecommunications industry. It has agreed to arrange interim financing to meet the working capital requirements of the parties prior to the closing.

Under a letter of intent that has been signed, the shareholders of Phoenix and US ONE, a privately held local exchange carrier, will each own 39.5 percent of the surviving entity. Resurgens will own 21 percent.
The companies intend to sign a definitive agreement within 30 days and close the deal within 120 days.

The companies also said that they are in the final stages of negotiations with two other long distance companies with combined annualised revenues in excess of $85 million that may become parties to the merger.

"Our business plan is a simple one," Phillips said in a statement. "Using as a base the companies who are parties to the announced merger, we intend to accumulate, through acquisitions and internal growth, a revenue base in excess of $1 billion over the next few years."

The surviving entity will serve more than 50,000 customers and have annualised revenues of about $85 million, without accounting for any revenues attributable to other possible acquisitions, the companies said.
